title: Contraction of monoidal ideals in a log regular sharp chart
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point, and let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Suppose that a chart $P\to M$ identifies $P$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$, and write $a:P\to(A,\cdot)$ for its structural map, with $P$ written additively. For every monoid ideal $J\subseteq P$ (a subset satisfying $J+P\subseteq J$, allowing the empty subset), let $JA=(a(j):j\in J)\subseteq A$. Then
$$a^{-1}(JA)=J.$$
Equivalently, a chart monomial $a(p)$ belongs to the ring ideal generated by the $a(j)$, $j\in J$, if and only if $p\in J$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 and its proof, printed p. 110: log ideals are recovered by contraction from their generated monoidal ideals; specialize at the geometric stalk in a chart identifying P with the sharp characteristic, so M_barx is P times A^units. The empty-ideal case also uses injectivity of alpha in the preceding conventions 3.4.1.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[P]$ and let $K=a^{-1}(JA)$. Because $a$ is multiplicative and $JA$ is an ideal of $A$, $K$ is a monoid ideal: if $p\in K$ and $q\in P$, then $a(p+q)=a(p)a(q)\in JA$. Every $j\in J$ lies in $K$, so $J\subseteq K$. The current chart definition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] identifies the chart monoid modulo the units of $A$ with the characteristic monoid; together with the sharp-chart lemma, this says that $P$ is finitely generated, integral and sharp and that every nonzero element of $P$ maps to a nonunit of the local ring $A$. Hence the ideal $\mathfrak m_P A$ generated by $P\setminus\{0\}$ is proper.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.1--3.4.3, printed pp. 110--111; reduce to a chart and use the injective structural map and sharp characteristic.

proof.text: Assume for contradiction that $J\subsetneq K$. The exact sequence of $R$-modules $JR\to KR\to KR/JR\to0$, after tensoring with $A$, is right exact. For each of the monoid ideals $J$ and $K$, the Tor-vanishing statement [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart] applied to $R/IR$ identifies $IR\otimes_R A$ with its multiplication image $IA\subseteq A$. Thus the first map has image $JA=KA$, so the right-exact sequence forces $(KR/JR)\otimes_R A=0$.

proof.text:
Since $J\subsetneq K$, some element of $K$ lies outside $J$. The monomials $e_q$ ($q\in P$) form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $R$, and for a monoid ideal $I$ the ideal $IR$ is the $\mathbf Z$-span of the $e_q$ with $q\in I$ (this span contains the generators and is stable under multiplication by monomials because $I+P\subseteq I$); so $KR/JR$ is free over $\mathbf Z$ on the classes of $e_k$, $k\in K\setminus J$. Because $P$ is finitely generated [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart], $R$ is a finite-type $\mathbf Z$-algebra and hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. A finite generating set of $KR$ consists of $\mathbf Z$-combinations of monomials from $K$, so finitely many $k_1,\dots,k_m\in K$ generate $KR$, and comparing coefficients of $e_k$ for $k\in K$ gives $K= igcup_i(k_i+P)$. proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m_P A$ is proper by step 1, since every generator $a(q)$ for $q\ne0$ is a nonunit in the local ring $A$. Therefore $A/\mathfrak m_P A\ne0$, so the surjection in step 3 contradicts the vanishing obtained in step 2. Thus $K=J$, which is exactly $a^{-1}(JA)=J$. The argument includes $J=\varnothing$: then $JA=(0)$, and any nonempty $K$ would give the same nonzero quotient contradiction.

mathlib_searches.query: For a log regular scheme, a monoid ideal is recovered by contraction of the ideal it generates in the structure sheaf.
Extension and contraction give a bijection between logarithmic ideals and monoidal ring ideals on log regular schemes.
In a sharp chart of a logarithmically regular local ring, a monomial belongs to an extended monoid ideal exactly when its exponent belongs to that ideal.

split_report.summary: Specialized Exposé VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 to the strict henselian stalk and wrote the chart proof. The contraction K is a monoid ideal containing J; Kato 6.1(ii) gives Tor-independence so tensor multiplication identifies monomial ideals with their generated ring ideals, and a minimal monomial generator of K outside J (Z[P] Noetherian) yields a quotient by the sharp monoid maximal ideal. Its tensor is A modulo the proper ideal generated by nonunit chart monomials, contradicting equality of generated ideals. The empty ideal is included. Added one statement-only Kato Tor-independence node; no Mathlib match.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the proof (1)--(2) ancestry of lem-trf-local-term-locality at Exposé VIII, 3.4.3: the monomial-ideal contraction input used by the regularity criterion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-353097cbe (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the delivery in full against ILO Exposé VIII 3.4.1–3.4.3 (pp. 110–111). The item's statement is right as the stalk form of 3.4.3, checked against the chart definition and the sharp-chart lemma; I tested it on P=0, N, N^2 and the empty J. The new statement-only node lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart is the stalk specialization of Kato 6.1(ii) as ILO quotes it (Kato himself is WANTED). It is true on small cases, has no duplicate in the DAG (rg for Kato/Tor/monoid ideal) and is not a restatement of the item. Steps 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Step 3 as delivered was false (E3): it claims the class of a 'minimal' p in K\J is killed by every nonzero monomial, which fails for J empty, K=P, the case the delivery says it covers, and for P=N^2, J=(x), K=P. It was also marked elementary although it needs Noetherianity. FIX: the corrected item in fixes/ rewrites step 3 as the source's quotient sentence written out. Z[P] is Noetherian (lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian, a Mathlib leaf), so K has finitely many monomial generators. Sharpness and integrality give a minimal generator p not in J and not in K+P^+. The functional e_p -> 1 is then an R-linear surjection onto R/m_P R = Z, and right exactness passes it to A/m_P A. proof_deps is now the union of the step uses.
